summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 1.5/28)

data.turoyo: Qayəm maškalle aʕlayna, lu qaymaqam, u qaymaqam ṭləblelan, azzano as sənʕatkar kulayna, l su qaymaqam. <...>
data.translation: Nun also beschwerten sie sich über uns beim Landrat. Der Landrat bestellte uns ein, wir Handwerker gingen alle zusammen zum Landrat. <...>

rationale: Adds explicit accused ʕal- and authority l- in a complete context; brings Preterit cell from four to five.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 66/33)

data.turoyo: Azza i kaftare, maškela su dahba. Əmmo: "Mḥəleli lu taʕlo xanǧar w šqile lišoni."
data.translation: Der Schakal aber ging hin und klagte bei der Hyäne: "Der Fuchs hat mir einen Dolchstoss versetzt und mir die Zunge weggenommen."

rationale: Unusual feminine weak-final Preterit maškela, not represented in existing masculine/plural contexts.

data.translation: <...> und er wagte es auch nicht, sich bei dem Onkel zu beklagen.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; a family addressee rather than a formal court.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 71/104)

data.translation: <...> aber während er seine Klage anbrachte, kam die alte Frau von den Elfen, den Fuchs zu suchen.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (64/273)

data.turoyo: Lu abro du šulṭono məlle: "Abro! Kobenux waʕd, d lo maškeno gab babi aʕlux w dʕar!
data.translation: Der Sultanssohn sagte: Mein Sohn! Ich verspreche dir, daß ich mich bei meinem Vater nicht über dich beklagen werde, kehre um!

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; authority gab and accused ʕal in the same proposition.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (Lahdo Traitor 2/70)

data.turoyo: <...> D əbʕat zux, zux maški d əbʕat l Awroppa, d əbʕat l Turkiya, d əbʕat lə gḏaʕno l ayko. <...>
data.translation: <...> And if you would like go, go and complain, and also to Europe, if you would like, and if you would like to Turkey, and if you would like, I don’t know where to. <...>

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell and variant maški; institutional destinations l-.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 68/74)

data.turoyo: Əmmo: "Ono ste, gnuleli ʕəsri qurš." Omər: "E, zoxu aškawu aʕle, əno gdoweno suhdo."
data.translation: "Auch mir hat er zwanzig Piaster gestolen." "Gut", sagte der Hund; "geht nur und klagt ihn an; ich will dabei als Zeuge auftreten."

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell and plural aškawu with explicit defendant.

summary: All supplied uses fit existing III.1. Distinguish complaint recipient/authority from person complained about: compare JTM 1.5/28 aʕlayna lu qaymaqam and 64/273 gab babi aʕlux. No gloss rewrite is needed to state these argument frames.
Reciprocal ʕal ḥḏoḏe occurs with active III forms throughout PrS. Reciprocal participants alone do not establish Detransitive morphology or a new sense.
Postverbal l-marked agents occur in PrS 24/5, 50/32, 71/105 and 73/90; an l-NP after this verb must not automatically be read as the judicial recipient.

Infectum serves ongoing background at PrS 71/104, prospective complaints and purpose/prevention clauses; Preterit gives completed complaint events. Feminine maškela at PrS 66/33 and Imperativ variants maški/aškawu add form coverage.
PrS page-style inherited references and text/verse labels are different systems. Clause matches do not by themselves justify replacing citations.
PrS 43/9 has no supplied German for its embedded complaint clause; PrS 62/102 German describes another action. Neither has been quoted as an added example.
Check full edition alignment for PrS 43/9, whose Turoyo block includes verse 10 but whose German stops earlier, and PrS 62/102–103 before quoting the complaint at /102.
Confirm the antecedent of gabe at PrS 51/20; it appears to anticipate Osman Pasha, rather than denote the person complained against.
Confirm the inherited PrS page-to-text/verse concordance and EL 33 = Hors 1/33; no automatic citation correction is proposed.
English typo: Than → Then.
rationale: The sentence describes the subsequent complaint; the temporal adverb is Then. The cited verse likewise places the complaint after the refusal.

summary: Institutional and family complaint recipients share the existing sense. Addressee may be gab-, l-, s- or b-, while ʕal- identifies the accused; b- can also mark venue.
Animals as litigants or authorities in fables extend participant type, without a separate legal or figurative sense.
